title: Quiet transit measurements of KIC 12557548 cluster in Kepler quarters 1 to 17 under tested shuffle models
abstract: We tested whether small transit flux deficits occur in groups for the known dusty planet KIC 12557548 b. We measured 1902 orbits from 17 public Kepler release 25 light curves. Quiet states are the lowest fifth of each quarter. The raw-flux test gives 102 adjacent quiet pairs. The exact expected counts are 69.45 for a quarter shuffle and 84.06 for a 30-orbit block shuffle. The permutation upper-tail probabilities are 0.00020 and 0.00360. The main off-transit control gives probabilities of 0.249 and 0.177. Both time halves reject the quarter shuffle, but the first half does not reject the block shuffle at 0.05. Raw and corrected flux give the same direction of the effect across three event widths. These tests measure time order beyond a depth correlation. They do not establish a dust survival time, a new object, or an independent telescope confirmation. The package includes all 17 raw files, hashes, per-orbit measurements, all 288 tests, an exact null-mean check, source code, and a figure.

display.caption: Measured transit flux deficits and null distributions for the adjacent quiet-pair count. The observed count is 102. Quiet means the lowest fifth of measurements in each quarter. The block null keeps counts within 30-orbit blocks.
